# Mutable Instruments DSP provenance

Author: Émilie Gillet. Original MIT copyright/permission notices are retained
in the source files. See their headers for the full license and disclaimer.

- Source: https://github.com/pichenettes/eurorack
- Pinned commit: f4cfa7697095a28d292bff758beb51deb49b5a86
- stmlib submodule: https://github.com/pichenettes/stmlib
- Pinned stmlib commit: e3bd7c9cc00e4364166f9905c0509b6ffd0535ec
- Retrieved 2026-10-25.

S7 compiles plaits/dsp/engine/fm_engine.cc, waveshaping_engine.cc,
virtual_analog_engine.cc and swarm_engine.cc (wavetable_engine.cc is no longer built), their
headers/dependencies, needed resources and stmlib pitch conversion tables.
Unused tables/code are removed by section garbage collection.

Vendored source edits:

1. plaits/dsp/dsp.h sets kCorrectedSampleRate to 48000
instead of 47872.34, compensating for Bluebox's sample rate rather than the
original Plaits hardware clock divider. The change is marked in that file.
2. plaits/dsp/engine/wavetable_engine.cc allocates all four 64-entry wave-map
banks (256 pointers), matching LoadUserData's loop. The pinned source allocated
only one bank (64 pointers). No waveform or rendering equation is changed.

3. S3a adds an immutable 256-pointer factory map in wavetable_engine.cc and
supports Init(nullptr) to use it without per-track RAM. Its pointer member is
read-only; LoadUserData skips the immutable mode. Allocator-backed initialization
retains the original mutable-map path, with the corrected 256-entry bound.
The factory map is bit-identical to LoadUserData(nullptr)'s original mapping.

4. S5 allows a null AUX pointer for Swarm: it skips the AUX clear and the
independent sine oscillator in SwarmVoice when only primary OUT is requested.
The Bluebox wrapper uses that path because AUX was already discarded. Primary
saw equations, all eight voices, waveform data and random progression are
unchanged. Full OUT/AUX rendering remains available to reference tests.

5. S6 extends the null-AUX path to FMEngine, VirtualAnalogEngine (variant 2),
WaveshapingEngine and WavetableEngine. With aux == nullptr they skip work that
only feeds AUX: FM's sub oscillator and its downsampler; VA's primary_ and
auxiliary_ oscillators; Waveshaping's triangle oscillator, fold_2 and sine;
Wavetable's quantized copy. Primary OUT arithmetic is unchanged and host/ARM
tests compare it bit for bit with S5. Passing a buffer keeps full AUX output.

The primary engine rendering equations and waveform data are otherwise unchanged.

Swarm uses the original stmlib Random implementation. The ARM linker binds its
single temporary state word to M7-only reserved backup SRAM at 0x388001b4;
each track explicitly seeds/saves its own RNG around Render. The host harness
links upstream random.cc normally. No writable flash static initialization is
required. The native eight SwarmVoice objects are owned by each track.

Cobalt adds its own MIDI/AR envelope/output/routing wrapper, low-pass filter,
triangle LFO and note-triggered modulation attack/decay envelope. Synth output is
not claimed to reproduce the entire Plaits module, its LPG or analog circuitry.
The primary output is duplicated as mono; AUX is not misrepresented as stereo.
Freestanding headers in src/freestanding supply only the facilities needed by
these selected sources, including placement new and hardware float math.

Cobalt is an independent project, not an official Mutable Instruments product.

S7 replaces the Plaits Wavetable engine slot with Cobalt's own Cluster engine
(src/cluster_engine.h, src/cluster_waves.h). It is independent code that only
uses the Plaits Engine interface, NoteToFrequency and stmlib's
ParameterInterpolator; its waves are generated by Cobalt's make_waves.py.
